scope: Design the operations intake and maintenance track that converts authenticated logs, error groups, traces, SLO alerts, dependency/security findings, and CI outcomes into a small set of evidence-backed work items. The boundary ends at a PLANNING-ready issue and, for a very small allowlist, invocation of an already approved reversible runbook. It does not let an RCA/coding agent patch production, publish a vulnerability into a public issue, decide product priority, change required checks, approve its own plan, or alter permissions/policy. Git stores desired taxonomy, routing, schemas, runbooks, and Project field mappings; actual Issues and Project v2 items/field values are remote GitHub state and require observed-state reconciliation, not claims that YAML itself is status.
current_capabilities: GitHub webhooks expose typed action payloads for workflow_run/check_run/check_suite, code_scanning_alert, dependabot_alert, secret_scanning_alert, deployment/deployment_status, issues and project_v2_item events. GitHub recommends subscribing only to needed events, validating a secret, responding within 10 seconds, asynchronous queueing, and using X-GitHub-Delivery as a delivery identifier; missed deliveries need an explicit redelivery process (https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks; payload catalog: https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads). Delivery identity is not the same as semantic incident identity.

The REST create-issue endpoint supports title/body/assignees/milestone/labels and fine-grained GitHub App/user/PAT use requires Issues:write; invalid/spam-like creation may return 422 (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues#create-an-issue). REST endpoints expose code-scanning, Dependabot, and secret-scanning alerts, but their token types, organization roles, and security permissions differ; therefore ingestion must use separate least-privilege adapters (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependabot/alerts; https://docs.github.com/en/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning).

Code scanning consumes SARIF. GitHub uses SARIF partialFingerprints to recognize logically identical results; missing fingerprints are synthesized on upload, and analysis/category changes can produce duplicate or closed/new alerts (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/integrating-with-code-scanning/sarif-support-for-code-scanning). This scanner identity should be retained, but cross-signal issue dedupe still belongs to the controller.

GitHub Projects supports built-in item/status automation and GraphQL mutations such as updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-built-in-automations; https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#updateprojectv2itemfieldvalue). These mutate remote objects addressed by node/field/option IDs. A repository mapping is desired configuration, not proof that the remote mutation succeeded.

GitHub Actions offers explicit GITHUB_TOKEN permissions and concurrency controls, but workflow_run is privileged: it can access secrets and write tokens even if the preceding workflow could not, and running untrusted code in that path can cause cache poisoning or unintended write/secret access; chains are limited to three levels (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions; https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run). Keep collection/untrusted diagnosis separate from publication.

Prometheus Alertmanager performs deduplication, grouping, routing, silencing, and inhibition (https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/alertmanager/). OpenTelemetry supplies logs/metrics/traces and a log model with TraceId/SpanId/resource/severity fields, while W3C Trace Context standardizes traceparent/tracestate propagation (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/; https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/; https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/). These enable correlation, not causal proof.
representative_systems: Use GitHub webhooks + REST/GraphQL as the repository control surface; OpenTelemetry/W3C Trace Context as the correlation substrate; the existing monitor and Alertmanager-like grouping/inhibition layer for paging/noise; GitHub code scanning/SARIF, Dependabot, secret scanning and Actions as source-specific adapters; Sentry-style issue fingerprints only as an example of upstream error grouping; and a durable controller database/outbox as the authoritative event-to-work ledger. Google SRE distinguishes pages, tickets and root cause and advises symptom-oriented alerting (https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/); NIST SP 800-61r3 frames detection, response and recovery inside governed cybersecurity risk management (https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r3/final). No reviewed platform is a complete, safe logs-to-autonomous-production-repair system.
primary_evidence: GitHub's webhook best practices require minimum subscriptions, secret validation, HTTPS, a response within 10 seconds, asynchronous processing when needed, event/action checks, recovery of missed deliveries, and X-GitHub-Delivery tracking: https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks and signature validation details: https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/validating-webhook-deliveries.

GitHub issue creation and REST rate limits show both the needed Issues:write capability and platform-wide/content-generation throttles: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/issues#create-an-issue and https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api.

GitHub security adapters have distinct alert endpoints and permission requirements: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/code-scanning/code-scanning, https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependabot/alerts, and https://docs.github.com/en/rest/secret-scanning/secret-scanning. SARIF partialFingerprints provide upstream result continuity but do not define a cross-tool work identity: https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/integrating-with-code-scanning/sarif-support-for-code-scanning.

Project v2 mutation and built-in automation docs establish that Project status is mutable remote state: https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#updateprojectv2itemfieldvalue and https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/automating-your-project/using-the-built-in-automations.

OpenTelemetry signals/log correlation and W3C Trace Context supply interoperable evidence identifiers: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/, https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/logs/data-model/, https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/.
Alertmanager documents dedupe/group/routing/silence/inhibition controls rather than creating one downstream record for each firing sample: https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/alertmanager/.
independent_evidence: Google SRE says alerts can target a ticket, email or pager and defines root cause separately; page on urgent user-visible symptoms rather than attempting to ticket every cause (https://sre.google/sre-book/monitoring-distributed-systems/). Its SLO workbook uses error-budget burn behavior, which supports persistence/multi-window qualification instead of raw threshold fan-out (https://sre.google/workbook/alerting-on-slos/).

ITBench tests diagnosis/remediation in realistic IT environments. The reported best cited configuration in the prior validated synthesis achieved 13.81% diagnosis pass@1 and 11.43% mitigation pass@1, with 0% on hard repair; task/environment definitions differ from production, but the result directly challenges general autonomous remediation claims (paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05352).

OWASP treats prompt injection and excessive agency as principal LLM risks. Telemetry, issue text, stack traces, commit messages and linked pages are untrusted data, so an LLM summary cannot authorize tools or override policy (https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/; https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/).

GitHub warns that a workflow_run job may gain secrets/write tokens and that untrusted code in it can cause cache poisoning or unintended write access (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run). This is counterevidence to a convenient single workflow that both analyzes arbitrary CI artifacts and writes issues/projects.

Google's automation chapter warns that automation has value and risks, including system-wide effects; it supports bounded, staged automation rather than treating runbook availability as sufficient authority (https://sre.google/sre-book/automation-at-google/).
metrics_and_limits: Platform limits are safety inputs, not throughput targets. GitHub says REST primary limits vary by authentication; a user is generally 5,000 requests/hour, and secondary content creation is generally no more than 80 content-generating requests/minute and 500/hour, with lower endpoint limits possible (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api). SARIF supports at most 25,000 results per run but includes only the top 5,000, so absence after truncation is not resolution (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/integrating-with-code-scanning/sarif-support-for-code-scanning). A webhook receiver must answer within 10 seconds. Locally measure, by source/service/severity: raw events, validated events, unique fingerprints, new/reopened/suppressed issues, precision after human adjudication, missed-impact rate, duplicate rate, time-to-triage, stale-open rate, recurrence, pages per incident, CI retry success, runbook success/abort/rollback, security disclosure leaks (target zero), and API/backlog p50/p95. Report denominators and confidence intervals; never reward issue count. Promotion requires a predeclared precision/miss trade-off, no worse user SLO/security outcomes, successful rollback drills, and zero unauthorized writes. Exact acceptable thresholds and sample sizes are repository-specific [uncertain].
recommended_design: Use a two-plane controller. The evidence plane validates/envelopes every source event, stores an immutable redacted raw reference, normalizes it, and updates a durable incident/work cluster. The authority plane applies deterministic policy and an outbox to create/update at most one planned issue per active fingerprint family. A fingerprint should combine tenant/repo, signal class, service/component, environment, stable detector/rule ID, normalized failure/error signature, affected dependency/advisory or CI workflow/job, and a versioned fingerprint algorithm; exclude transient timestamps, trace IDs and secret values. Add topology/deploy/trace links only as evidence. Route paging separately from backlog creation: SLO/user-impact/security urgency determines an incident/page; durable actionable defects become planned issues; informational/transient noise is retained or sampled. LLMs may summarize, cluster candidates, and rank hypotheses, but deterministic rules decide publication, privacy, permissions, runbook eligibility and stop conditions. Use a security-private queue/advisory repository for secrets/vulnerabilities. Never put raw secrets or embargoed findings into ordinary issues. Code defects always return through PLANNING -> READY -> PR -> protected CI -> canary. Only a signed, versioned, idempotent, bounded, recently drilled runbook may execute automatically, using a separate short-lived operations identity and independent postconditions.
state_and_event_contract: EventEnvelope v1 = {event_id, delivery_id, source, source_event_id, source_action, tenant, repo, received_at, occurred_at, producer_version, payload_schema, payload_sha256, signature_valid, redaction_class, raw_ref, correlation:{trace_id,span_id,deploy_id,artifact_digest,head_sha,workflow_run_id,alert_number}, classification}. Unique(source, delivery_id) prevents delivery replay; unique(source, source_event_id, source_revision) handles source updates. NormalizedSignal v1 = {signal_id, kind:error|slo|ci|code_scan|dependency|secret|deploy, detector_id, detector_version, service, component, environment, severity, status:firing|resolved|dismissed|fixed|reopened, normalized_signature, first_seen,last_seen,count,evidence_refs,privacy,owner_hint}. Fingerprint vN and cluster_id are explicit and migrations preserve aliases. Cluster lifecycle: OBSERVED -> QUALIFYING -> SUPPRESSED | TRIAGE; TRIAGE -> INCIDENT (urgent) and/or PROPOSED_ISSUE; PROPOSED_ISSUE -> PLANNING -> READY only through the repository planning gate; active clusters become MITIGATED then RESOLVED_PENDING_COOLDOWN then CLOSED. Recurrence reopens the same issue when semantics/ownership remain stable; materially new cause/scope creates a linked successor. SECURITY_QUARANTINE and HUMAN_INCIDENT are terminal-to-human paths. Every action has action_id/cluster_id/desired_revision/attempt, compare-and-swap revision, per-cluster/resource lock, capped retry, and outbox/inbox records. Reconciliation reads GitHub by stored issue node/number and Project item/field IDs, compares remote observed revision/field values to desired mapping, and: repairs safe controller-owned drift; imports allowed human changes; or records DRIFT_CONFLICT and stops. It never assumes an API 2xx means all later Project mutations completed.
repository_artifacts: .github/ops/intake.schema.json, signal.schema.json, cluster.schema.json, work-item.schema.json and examples/: versioned JSON Schemas plus compatibility tests.
.github/ops/sources.yaml: allowlisted GitHub webhook actions, OTel/monitor endpoints, detector IDs/versions, privacy class, owners and fail-open/fail-closed choice; no credentials.
.github/ops/fingerprints.yaml and normalization/: ordered field rules, regex/parser versions, ignored volatile tokens, alias/migration rules, golden fixtures and collision/split policy.

.github/ops/routing.yaml, noise-policy.yaml and sla.yaml: service ownership, severity floor, persistence/hysteresis, group_wait/group_interval/repeat/cooldown, quotas, maintenance windows, suppressions with owner/reason/expiry, SLO/error-budget conditions and escalation schedule.

.github/ops/issue-template.md plus issue-mapping.yaml: stable marker (<!-- ops-cluster:... -->), evidence/provenance, user impact, first/last seen, counts, current hypothesis explicitly labeled, recent change, owner, runbook, privacy, acceptance/verification, rollout/rollback, links, and label mapping.

.github/ops/project-desired.yaml: Project owner/number and symbolic field/option names plus desired mappings. .github/ops/project-lock.json: last resolved node IDs/schema hash only as a cache. Neither is actual status; controller state stores last-observed remote values/revisions and drift decisions.

.github/ops/runbooks/<id>.yaml and docs/runbooks/<id>.md: signed/versioned ID, exact signature/risk, parameters and bounds, preconditions, resource/concurrency key, credential profile, commands/API verbs, timeout, postconditions, compensator/rollback, evidence retention, last drill, owner, expiry and mandatory-human conditions.

.github/workflows/ops-policy-ci.yml validates schemas/golden fingerprints/runbooks; ops-reconcile.yml may reconcile repository/Project metadata using a pinned reusable workflow and least privilege. Do not process attacker-controlled artifacts in the privileged publisher job.

policy/ops.rego (or equivalent) and tests/: permission/action decision rules. docs/operations/{architecture,threat-model,incident-escalation,rollback,drift-recovery}.md; migrations/; evals/ops/{cases,holdout-manifest}.jsonl; CODEOWNERS requiring operations/security review for policy, workflows, schemas and runbooks.
workflow_steps: 1. Receive only allowlisted events. Verify GitHub HMAC before parsing; enforce body/time limits; record delivery ID/hash; redact at ingestion; acknowledge inside 10 seconds and queue durably. Invalid/oversized/schema-unknown events quarantine and alert the controller owner, with no GitHub write.

2. Normalize using a pinned adapter. Fetch authoritative source state when webhook payload is partial. Security findings enter a private queue. Add trace/deploy/SHA/artifact/topology links, but preserve provenance and mark missing/truncated evidence.

3. Compute versioned exact fingerprint, then optional similarity candidates. Acquire the cluster lock and reduce events deterministically. Upstream Alertmanager/Sentry/SARIF group IDs are evidence, not universal identity.

4. Apply maintenance-window, inhibition, expiry-bound suppression, persistence/hysteresis, rate/quota and SLO-impact policy. Never equate silence with resolved; suppressed clusters remain counted and sampled for audit. Burst overflow creates one digest/overflow incident rather than silent drops.

5. Enrich with CODEOWNERS/service catalog, recent deploy/config/dependency changes, last passing CI, existing open/closed issues, known runbook and current Project state. An agent may draft a cited summary and ranked hypotheses; facts, inference and missing evidence are separate.

6. Deterministic policy chooses DROP_WITH_AUDIT, HOLD, UPDATE_CLUSTER, CREATE_PRIVATE_SECURITY_CASE, CREATE/REOPEN_PLANNED_ISSUE, PAGE/INCIDENT, or REQUEST_RUNBOOK. The outbox publisher searches by stable marker and stored node ID, then creates or patches idempotently. It comments only on meaningful transitions/bounded digests, not every sample.

7. Reconcile issue labels/assignee and Project item/status as separate remote writes. Read after write. If head/spec/field schema has drifted, record conflict and stop rather than overwrite a human or invent IDs. PLANNING is the intake destination; READY is not granted by observability.

8. For a matched runbook, verify signed version, fresh drill, incident/action id, lock, current desired/observed state, freeze/error budget, bounded resource and independent postconditions. Execute once using a short-lived scoped identity. Failure, ambiguity, missing/conflicting telemetry or rollback failure stops at HUMAN_INCIDENT.

9. On resolved source state, verify user/SLO recovery and wait a source-specific cooldown. Update evidence, close only if no active aliases remain, and link deploy/fix/rollback. Recurrence reopens or creates a linked successor by declared policy.

10. Nightly reconciliation scans webhook gaps, dead letters, source-vs-cluster-vs-issue-vs-Project drift, expired suppressions/runbooks, orphaned items and API failures. Operators use documented replay from immutable envelopes; replay never repeats a completed action because action IDs and source revisions are durable.
human_gates: Humans must approve: public handling/disclosure of secret or embargoed vulnerability data; new detector/fingerprint/routing/noise policy; any READY/product priority decision; issue closure when evidence conflicts or customer/security obligations exist; a novel, destructive, stateful, cross-region/global, data/schema, auth/crypto, customer-communication or Sev-1/2 action; rollback failure; scope/permission expansion; workflow or required-check edits; and every promotion of an agent/model/prompt/runbook/policy. Bind approval to an immutable proposal hash containing cluster evidence revision, plan/spec, runbook/policy version, exact resources/parameters, credentials profile, postconditions and expiry. New evidence, changed parameters, changed commit/runbook, expired time or remote drift invalidates approval. Emergency break-glass requires named incident commander, narrow time-bound identity, logged rationale, two-person confirmation where feasible, kill switch and post-incident review. The proposing/diagnosing agent cannot approve, grant permissions, dismiss security alerts, edit audit evidence or change the gate that judges it.
security_and_failure_modes: Threats: spoofed/replayed webhooks; prompt injection in logs/issues/commit text; parser bombs and secret/PII leakage; adversarial fingerprint collisions that hide incidents or splits that flood issues; stale/out-of-order resolve events; GitHub/App token theft; workflow_run privilege escalation/cache poisoning; SSRF through evidence links; false RCA; poisoned runbook retrieval; API partial failure; Project field deletion/renaming; rate-limit storms; suppression without expiry; feedback loops in which bot comments trigger itself; automatic dismissal of a true security alert; and autonomous policy weakening. Mitigate with HMAC and constant-time verification, delivery/source uniqueness, bounded parsing, schema allowlists, redaction/DLP before persistence and LLM, opaque evidence references, egress allowlists, pinned dependencies/actions, separate receiver/reader/publisher/project/runbook identities, explicit token permissions, environment protection, non-LLM policy proxy, signed reviewed runbooks, per-resource locks, outbox/read-after-write, circuit breakers/backoff/dead letters, source-tagged recursion filters, quotas/overflow summaries, expiring suppressions with audits, and a global kill switch. Fail closed for auth, privacy, security writes, production action and missing postconditions; fail operationally visible (not silently) for enrichment/Project sync. A GitHub issue may contain untrusted Markdown/URLs and is never a command. Follow GitHub secure-use guidance (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions) and OWASP prompt-injection/excessive-agency controls.
validation_and_tests: Contract tests replay recorded, redacted fixtures for every allowed webhook action and API version; reject bad HMAC, duplicate delivery, oversize, malformed JSON, missing fields, unknown action and out-of-order update. Property tests prove reducer idempotency/commutativity where promised.

Golden fingerprint tests cover timestamp/path/PID/UUID normalization, same-defect grouping, distinct-service/cause separation, scanner partialFingerprints, dependency advisory aliases, CI matrix jobs, algorithm migration aliases, collision and cardinality attacks. Compare against human-adjudicated production samples with denominators.

State-machine/model tests exercise every legal/illegal transition, CAS conflict, lease expiry, dead letter, retry budget, recursion prevention, reopen/cooldown/supersede, suppression expiry, webhook gap/backfill and crash after each outbox boundary.

GitHub integration tests run against a disposable organization/repository/Project: create issue once under duplicate delivery, recover from 201 followed by crash, handle 403/404/409/422/429/5xx, rename/delete a Project field, remove an item, observe human edits, exhaust rate limits, read after write and verify DRIFT_CONFLICT rather than clobbering.

Permission tests demonstrate receiver cannot write GitHub, triage reader cannot create issues, publisher cannot read secrets or mutate workflows, Project reconciler has only required Project access, agent has no production credential, and only runbook executor gets short-lived bounded verbs. Include fork/untrusted artifact and workflow_run cache-poison simulations.

Privacy/security tests seed canary secrets/PII, malicious Markdown/tool instructions, huge traces, poisoned URLs and embargoed alerts; assert no public issue/model/export leak and no command execution. Audit logs must reconstruct who/what/version/why for every transition.

Runbook chaos drills inject stale telemetry, lock contention, timeout, partial action, postcondition failure, lost acknowledgment and failed compensator. Only known reversible cases may pass; all ambiguity must stop/escalate. Validate rollback RTO on a canary resource.

Shadow evaluation compares suggested clusters/issues to human triage. Canary by service/signal type with predeclared duplicate, precision, missed-impact, on-call-load, SLO, cost and rollback thresholds. Keep blinded temporal holdouts; the agent cannot edit cases or approve promotion.
operational_maintenance: Run continuous queue age/dead-letter/signature-failure/API-rate/redaction-drop/reconciliation-drift and publisher-loop dashboards. Daily: recover webhook delivery gaps, reconcile active source alerts to clusters/issues and Project observed state, retry safe idempotent outbox entries, and report overflow. Weekly: review false merges/splits, stale PLANNING items, orphan Project items, expired silences/exceptions/runbooks, public-data leaks, token use and sampled suppressed events. Monthly: rotate/test credentials, update adapters against versioned GitHub schemas, re-resolve symbolic Project IDs, rerun golden/eval/chaos suites, audit owners/SLAs and drill rollback/kill switch. Fingerprint migrations run shadow first, generate a merge/split impact report, preserve old aliases and require approval; never bulk-close by the new key alone. Back up controller DB/raw-reference index/outbox and test point-in-time restore. Recovery order is stop publishers/executors, preserve evidence, restore ledger, replay envelopes, reconcile source and GitHub, then re-enable one source. Project drift policy is explicit: controller-owned fields may be repaired; human-owned priority/approval is imported or conflicts; unknown/destructive drift stops. Upgrades to workflows/actions are pinned, reviewed and rolled out canary-first. Postmortems create owned improvement proposals/eval cases, never direct self-modification.
maturity_and_uncertainty: Mature/solved components: authenticated webhook intake, durable queues/outbox/idempotency, source-specific alert APIs, SARIF result continuity, Alertmanager-style grouping/inhibition/silencing, OTel/W3C correlation, GitHub issue creation and remote Project mutation. Conditional and repository-specific: useful cross-source fingerprints, auto-close/reopen policy, ownership inference, SLO thresholds, CI flake classification and deduplicated planning quality; these require labeled local data and ongoing audits. Experimental: LLM cross-signal clustering and RCA. Unsupported by reviewed evidence: broad autonomous diagnosis-to-production repair or an agent that changes/approves its permissions, policy, runbooks, evaluator or promotion. ITBench's low pass@1 is strong caution but not a direct production estimate. GitHub cloud feature names, permission details, Project GraphQL behavior and rate limits can change by 2026-09-13; integration tests must pin the API version and live documentation must be rechecked [uncertain]. No independent controlled denominator was found for this exact end-to-end GitHub issue-maintenance design [uncertain].
implementation_recommendation: MVP (4-6 weeks): connect one high-value SLO/error source plus GitHub Actions failures; deploy HMAC receiver, Postgres inbox/outbox/cluster ledger, versioned exact fingerprints, privacy partition, ownership/routing/noise rules, one PLANNING issue template and a nightly drift reconciler. Keep Project sync proposal/dry-run first; human triage approves every new/reopened/closed issue; no remediation. Stage 2: add code scanning/Dependabot/secret-scanning private adapters, cooldown maintenance, symbolic Project mapping with observed-state/conflict UI, and shadow LLM summaries. Stage 3: enable deterministic low-risk issue publication only for signal classes that meet local precision/miss/on-call thresholds; retain sampled review and automatic circuit breaker. Stage 4: permit one or two versioned, bounded, reversible, recently drilled runbooks (for example abort a canary or disable an already approved flag), never novel code, and require independent SLO recovery plus automatic escalation. Stage 5: propose improvements from false merge/split/incident data, evaluate offline/holdout, human-approve and canary; agents cannot alter gates or approve promotion. Core decision: build a small durable reconciliation controller around existing monitoring and GitHub, not a bot workflow that creates an issue per event and not an autonomous remediation agent.

conflicts: GitHub/SARIF/Sentry-style systems offer alert/error grouping, while cross-source operations needs an incident/work identity. There is no real contradiction: upstream fingerprints are detector-local and can be inputs, not the controller's semantic key. GitHub Projects looks automatable and configuration can live in Git, but the authoritative Project item/field values remain remote mutable state; resolve symbolic names to IDs and reconcile observed drift rather than calling YAML 'status as code.' Vendor RCA/autofix surfaces may report strong results, while ITBench reports low diagnosis/mitigation and zero hard-repair performance in its tested setup; datasets, tools, labels and outcome definitions differ, so neither licenses production autonomy. Noise reduction can lower on-call load but aggressive grouping/silencing can hide distinct incidents; measure both duplicate precision and missed-impact/false-merge rates and retain expiring auditable suppressions. A workflow_run publisher is convenient after CI, but GitHub explicitly warns it gains secrets/write access and untrusted artifacts can poison it; use a minimal parser/evidence boundary and a separate publisher rather than merging trust zones. Auto-closing when a source alert resolves is tempting, but SARIF truncation, missing telemetry and scanner rekeys mean 'not present' can be unknown; require explicit resolved/fixed state plus cooldown and reconciliation.
confidence: Overall: high for the architecture boundary, GitHub/API/OTel/Alertmanager capabilities, event authenticity/idempotency, least privilege, Project reconciliation requirement and proposal-first remediation. Medium for the exact cross-source fingerprint fields, close/reopen thresholds, local noise reduction and staged timing because they depend on telemetry quality and repository topology. Low for general LLM RCA and autonomous mitigation effectiveness; independent evidence is sparse and ITBench is unfavorable. Claim confidence is marked [uncertain] for future documentation drift and quantitative local promotion thresholds.
